alex: Heads up — I'm seeing a ~15-25% p95 latency regression on mistral-8x7b for short chat workloads after yesterday's kernel-selector deploy. Short sequences (~200 tokens) spike at rollout boundaries; traces show fallback to a generic tiled matmul path around sequence ~1024. p50/p95 numbers from production trace: p50 38ms -> 42ms, p95 95ms -> 120ms. Any ideas? :thinking:
maria: Can you paste the perf dump + kernel names from the trace? Also which batch sizes and sliding-window config?@leo might be relevant here.
alex: Quick paste from one of the traced requests (sanitized):
```
batch_size=1, seq_len=198, sliding_window=512,stride=512
kernel_choice: mistral_opt_kv_kernel_v2 -> fallback matmul_generic_tile
kv_evictions: 0
kv_ptr: 2048 -> 1 (wrap observed)
memcpy_host_to_device: 12MB
latency_breakdown_ms: kernel(78), memcpy(18), overhead(24)
```
leo: That kv_ptr wrap is a smoking gun. If kv pointer wraps (max_pos mismatch or RoPE scaling causing effective pos>=max_pos), the selector sees a non-monotonic seq distribution and chooses the safe generic kernel. We've seen this before when model max_position_embeddings != runtime max_pos. Also check RoPE scaling ordering — if we apply scaling after mask/stride adjustments it can create apparent large positions.
jen: I reproduced locally. With a sliding_window stride of 512 and starting prompt length ~1536, the pointer increments at step 2049 -> becomes 1 which trips our selector heuristic (we treat any seq decrease as a fallback condition). Repro command: `TEST_SEQ=1536 STRIDE=512 ./bench_mistral.sh --model mistral-8x7b --sliding-window $STRIDE --steps 8`. Observed selector log: `seq_dist_shock=true` then fallback.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: detected deploy `selector-v3` by @ci on 1871999800 affecting pool `prod-mistral-8x7b` — rolling update completed 1872000100.
maria: Short-term mitigations: 1) pin kernel selector to previous release on the affected pool (roll back selector-v3) 2) force runtime config `max_position_embeddings=4096` for this model group (overrides model config) 3) set a rope_scale_override=0.9 as a temporary hedge. Longer-term: update selector to detect wrapped KV pointers and treat them as long-seq rather than signal to fallback to slow kernel; add a CV test that simulates pointer wrap.
leo: Note: rope_scale_override will change logits slightly — need to run a quick eval on our canary promptset. But it's faster than global rollback. Also we should add a kernel-selector metric to count "seq_monotonicity_violations" so we can alert before p95 moves.
alex: OK. Plan: rollback selector-v3 on prod-mistral-8x7b now, enable max_pos override + rope_scale_override on the pool, run canary eval, then deploy patched selector that ignores single-step pointer wrap if it's < wrap_threshold. Who will take rollback + configs?
maria: I'll handle the rollback and config flip. tagging ops: @jen can you run the canary eval and post diffs (latency + quality) within the hour?
jen: On it. I'll run bench + eval and post results here. early note: local eval showed negligible quality delta at rope_scale=0.9 but latency p95 returned to baseline when forcing max_pos=4096.
alex: Great — thanks. Once we have canary green we'll coordinate a safe redeploy. Please also add a short perf test that simulates max_pos wrap to our nightly CI.
maria: adding ticket -> INF-1729 (will update). :white_check_mark:
